newsitem.title: UK: Costain revamps as losses rise.
newsitem.headline: Costain revamps as losses rise.

text.p: Troubled British engineering and construction firm Costain Group on Tuesday announced 52 million pounds ($86 million) of asset sales and top board changes as it struggled to refocus amid greater-than-expected losses.

The group said it was selling its U.S. coal units to Rencoal Inc of the U.S. for 28.6 million pounds and its one-third stake in the Spitalfields development site in London to Malaysia's Metacorp for 23.4 million pounds.
"Since the announcement of its interim results, the group has become aware of losses significantly greater than forecast," the company said in a statement.

Costain, which clinched a last-ditch survival refinancing in July before plunging deeper into the red, said the sale of its loss-making U.S. coal arm represented the final stage of its planned exit from U.S. mining.

The company, whose shares have been suspended since November 7, said that following the financial restructuring and asset sales, current joint deputy chairman Azman Firdaus bin Shafii would replace Sir Christopher Benson as chairman.
Alan Lovell also "considers it is appropriate to step down," Costain added. But it said he would stay with the group until a successor had been appointed.
Worse than anticipated geological conditions had hit production at its U.S. Coal unit, which Costain said would result in an 11 million pound lower trading result than expected.

Its Middle East construction businesses had also slipped further into the red and the company said it expected full year losses to be be 4.0 million pounds higher than forecast when it reported half year results about three months ago.

Costain, which was on the brink of administrative receivership this summer when it told investors that a 73 million pound refinancing was its last chance of survival, reported a 19.2 million pound first-half loss.

The company, which has not paid a dividend since November 1991, said its shares were unlikely to begin trading again until after the completion of the U.S. Coal sale, targeted for the end of December. ($1=.6047 Pound)
